title: Knowledge check: Building Applications with Nuxt

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Building Applications with Nuxt”?
options: Assume window and document exist during every server render.
Share mutable module-scope user state across all requests.
Use random values in initial markup and assume hydration will always match.
Keep server and initial client output deterministic, isolate mutable state per request, and avoid browser-only globals during server rendering.
questions.answer_key: Keep server and initial client output deterministic, isolate mutable state per request, and avoid browser-only globals during server rendering.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Building Applications with Nuxt directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Data fetching conventions”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Assume JSON parsing proves the HTTP response was successful.
Let the oldest request overwrite results for the latest input.
Model pending, success, empty, and failure states; check HTTP status and prevent stale requests from overwriting newer user intent.
Treat every fetch response as a successful business result.
questions.answer_key: Model pending, success, empty, and failure states; check HTTP status and prevent stale requests from overwriting newer user intent.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Data fetching conventions”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Building Applications with Nuxt” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
